subject: Objects
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 9.3.6 'The same calling convention shall be in effect for the invocation as is in effect for the invoked method' -> OK §9.3.6 2)). WiseOwl COBOL provides exactly one convention: ENTRY-CONVENTION accepts only COBOL (non-COBOL names refused COBOL2385, adjudicated in the entry-convention-clause subject), and >>CALL-CONVENTION is recognized-and-ignored with a documented single-convention disposition (docs/CONFORMANCE.md, 'Recognized-and-ignored compiler directives (§7.3)': 'CALL uses the single .NET managed calling convention'). The invocation's and the method's conventions are therefore always the same one, and the condition is satisfied by construction. Probe out/probe/objects-p1/cc.cob: >>CALL-CONVENTION XYZ before INVOKE R "M" compiled and ran M-OK — consistent with the documented disposition (§7.3.9.3 GR2 b) leaves call-convention-name-1's meaning to the implementor). Vacuous today; it becomes a live check the day a second convention is provided. Test-needed (nothing observable to golden beyond the documented disposition). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO is an ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduction; absent from 1985 — probe p1.cob at --std 85 is refused COBOL0900)
